transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-06 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Ross (Redwood) - Carlos Diaz, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor (Nimbus)

00:00 Maya: okay everyone good, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. we'll jump right into the benchmark slides, we had a few updates since last week.
00:15 Carlos: yep, thanks Maya. quick note, Priya's on for infra questions, Carlos will cover ML perf.
00:32 Ethan: cool, i'll start with the numbers we ran friday night, so baseline provider (they're running a mix of A100 clusters and some older VMs) — their median token latency at our 4k sequence profile was around 110ms per token, and p95 around 420ms. throughput for the 8-concurrent clients test was ~340 tokens/sec.
01:05 Priya: is that with batching on their end or single-instance?
01:09 Ethan: that's their standard setup, looks like a small batch size of 4; we saw some queuing.
01:20 Ethan: For Redwood running the same model variant unquantized on an rtx-like cluster we saw median ~85ms, p95 ~280ms, throughput ~470 tokens/sec with continuous batching and our kv cache warm. so median improved ~22%, throughput ~38% higher.
01:45 Carlos: wow that's promising. what's the cold start delta?
01:48 Ethan: cold-starts were noisy — 700-900ms tail on first requests for big contexts. we ran a warmed flow too and tail came down to ~300-350ms. so caching and warmers matter a lot.
02:10 Maya: just to interject, this is measured across our hosted pool with autoscaling; if you want dedicated capacity the p95s are even tighter because we avoid noisy neighbors, though cost goes up.
02:26 Liam: can you quantify "tighter"?
02:29 Ethan: in early dedicated runs p95 dropped to about 220-250ms for the same profile; p99 around 420ms. again these are with continuous batching and quantization disabled.
02:50 Priya: you're mentioning quantization — did you also test 4-bit or int8?
02:55 Ethan: yes we ran q4 and int8 runs; q4 had a small median increase (~5-10ms) but throughput went up about 10-15%. int8 in our bench gave best cost tradeoff but increased mismatches on a small eval set — i.e. slight quality delta. we have the eval diffs in the spreadsheet.
03:22 Carlos: that's critical for us, accuracy drop is sensitive. can you share the eval prompts?
03:28 Maya: yes we'll include the eval prompt set and the diff heatmaps.
03:34 Ethan: note there are transcription artifacts there is a false positive in one of our earlier notes where it said "kv cash" instead of kv cache, lol.
03:50 Priya: networking question — are these numbers with TLS termination on the host or inside the VPC? our baseline has some extra hop to the internal proxy.
03:58 Ethan: all hosted numbers were with TLS termination at the public edge, so yes you might see extra ~20-30ms in your internal setup. Dedicated/private deployment with VPC mode removes that hop.
04:15 Priya: okay that explains part of the delta. can we reproduce the baseline provider network topology?
04:20 Maya: we can mimic it in our dedicated pilot, we'll schedule the VPC deep-dive to align routing.
04:28 Carlos: given your numbers, what's your recommended pilot configuration?
04:32 Maya: recommended: start with Redwood hosted to validate accuracy and batching configs, then move to a small Dedicated pool for steady-state measurements with VPC peering to mimic your production network. enable kv prefix caching for repeated queries and try q4 quantization in a canary.
04:50 Liam: cost question — how much more for Dedicated?
04:53 Maya: depends on commit but ballpark for your pilot sized footprint it's about 1.6x hosted list for reserved capacity, but per-token cost can be lower once batching and caching reduce ops. we'll send exact numbers.
05:10 Carlos: the tail latency at p99 concerns me — even if median is lower, spikes can cause poor UX. any mitigations?
05:16 Ethan: yes, several: 1) isolate workloads in Dedicated, 2) allow fallback to a smaller model variant for spikes (we can configure automatic fallback), 3) warm pools for expected windows, 4) tune batching timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking. we also expose per-route SLOs in console for alerting.
05:43 Priya: how effective was the fallback in your stress test?
05:47 Ethan: fallback reduced p99 from ~900ms to ~420ms in our sim; quality reduced slightly but we configured thresholds to only trigger for overloaded nodes.
06:05 Carlos: on the numbers you shared, there were several runs — can you point me to raw logs?
06:09 Ethan: yes, spreadsheet link in chat with logs and the raw Prometheus exports. i'll drop the artifact after the call.
06:18 Maya: quick note on methodology — we used realistic seq length distribution you shared last week: 60% <1k, 30% 1k-4k, 10% >4k. For the 16k experiments we did a separate run and saw more pronounced tails, expectedly.
06:36 Priya: did you vary batch windows? what batch timeout was used?
06:39 Ethan: default continuous batching timeout of 8ms; we tried 4/8/16ms. 4ms improved p95 slightly at lower throughput; 16ms helped throughput but increased median by ~12ms.
06:55 Carlos: any differences on attention optimizations? our baseline says they use some fused kernels but maybe not the newest ones.
06:59 Ethan: we included kernel selection tweaks in our runner; Redwood runtime picks kernels by seq length and hardware. that gave us an extra ~7-10% perf on mid-length sequences.
07:18 Liam: security/compliance — we need SOC2 and KMS integration for keys. did you share your corp security deck?
07:23 Maya: yes sent last week, but i'll re-send the SOC2 cert and our KMS/HSM integration notes. dedicated/private includes customer-managed KMS.
07:33 Priya: logging and audit retention?
07:36 Ethan: we can configure audit log retention per contract; we export to your S3 and ship via syslog.
07:44 Carlos: ok good. any notable regressions vs baseline on quality metrics?
07:48 Ethan: small differences for int8 quantization on a narrow eval subset; q4 was mostly within acceptable deltas. we flagged the exact prompts where divergence occurred.
08:03 Maya: next steps recap: we'll share the full benchmark spreadsheet, raw logs, and the quant plan; Ethan will rerun the 16k cold/cold-start tests and include the Prometheus dumps; schedule VPC deep-dive.
08:20 Priya: timeline sounds good. i want the 16k p95/p99 runs by monday so we can decide on canary.
08:26 Carlos: for the pricing we need the delta for a 3-month pilot and an annual reserved estimate.
08:30 Maya: noted — i'll include both scenarios.
08:34 Liam: are there any blockers you see for scaling to our expected 500 concurrent users?
08:38 Ethan: main concerns are network concurrency and warm pool sizing; we'll propose autoscale policies and recommended pool sizes; also recommend session affinity to reduce context re-loads.
08:52 Priya: one last nit — your transcript earlier said "kv cash" which confused me.
08:55 Ethan: sorry for that, transcription typo, meant kv cache.
09:00 Maya: cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with artifacts and set the VPC deep-dive for next week.

Meeting end: ~45m. Artifacts shared: benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx (link), prom-export.tar.gz (link), quantization_plan.md (link).
